messages:
alex: Heads up — onboarding sample in /examples/chat started failing in Cloudflare Workers after we pushed the exports-map change this morning. Works on Node locally though. Logs below.

maria: @alex can you paste the package.json exports block and the exact error? which SDK build are you on? :eyes: 

alex: SDK is redwood-js-sdk@1.4.0. exports block from package.json: 

```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "types": "./dist/index.d.ts",
    "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/index.cjs"
  },
  "./server": "./dist/server.cjs"
}
```

Error seen in Worker runtime: 

```
TypeError [ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION]: Cannot use import statement outside a module
    at new NodeError (internal/errors.js:...)
    at Loader.defaultLoad (internal/modules/esm/loader.js:...)
    at async Loader.getModuleJob (internal/modules/esm/loader.js:...)
```

We think something in the exports map resolution is causing the worker to pull the wrong entry (CJS vs ESM).

sam: Cloudflare/Wranger V8 runtime expects ESM. If the resolver picks the require path for some subpath import, you'll get this. Did the bundler rewrite imports or is wrangler using native ESM resolution?

maria: also are any imports using deep subpaths like `redwood-js-sdk/server`? that would hit the "./server" mapping which is CJS and will definitely blow up in Workers.

alex: the sample imports `import { start } from "redwood-js-sdk"` only. But some transitive dep in the example does `require('redwood-js-sdk/server')` for SSR in Node-only flow. Locally the dev server never hits that path but the worker packaging apparently pulls it into the bundle and then runtime tries to evaluate the CJS file.

leo: quick diagnosis: exports map currently exposes a bare "./server" subpath with a CJS file. In bundlers that do static analysis, that subpath can be referenced indirectly and end up being included in the worker bundle. Worker then throws on mixed formats. We should provide an explicit ESM edge entry or mark subpath as node-only.

maria: Agreed. Two options: 1) Add a dedicated edge entrypoint in exports (e.g., "./edge": { "import": "./dist/index.mjs" }) and update examples to use it for worker builds, or 2) change package to advertise ESM-first by moving the ESM file to the default import target so bundlers prefer that. Option 1 is safer.

alex: I can try adding an "./edge" mapping and republishing a patch. Any objections?

sam: go for it. also add a small note in SDK README about which subpaths are Node-only (server) vs ESM (browser/edge). Will reduce future surprises.

maria: patch suggestion (quick diff):

```diff
@@ package.json
 "exports": {
-  ".": {
-    "types": "./dist/index.d.ts",
-    "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
-    "require": "./dist/index.cjs"
-  },
-  "./server": "./dist/server.cjs"
+  ".": {
+    "types": "./dist/index.d.ts",
+    "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
+    "require": "./dist/index.cjs"
+  },
+  "./server": "./dist/server.cjs",
+  "./edge": {
+    "import": "./dist/index.mjs"
+  }
 }
```

And bump to 1.4.1. I'll also add README blurb and a unit test that bundles examples with wrangler to catch regressions.

leo: Note for release: we should also run a quick smoke for Deno/Cloudflare/Netlify edge to ensure their resolvers pick the import path. Different runtimes/bundlers have subtle resolver behavior.

ci-bot: CI: Published redwood-js-sdk@1.4.1 — smoke tests: wrangler (pass), node (pass), bundle-size (ok). Release notes: "exports: add ./edge export for ESM edge runtimes; clarify server-only subpath". See changelog: https://internal/release/1.4.1

alex: confirmed — onboarding example in Workers now boots cleanly after the upgrade. Thanks y'all. :tada:

maria: leaving a follow-up PR to annotate the example packaging config and add a note in the migration guide about export-map pitfalls for edge runtimes.

leo: filing a small eng-runtime ticket to add an automated check in our SDK release CI that runs an edge-bundle step. assigning to @maria.

sam: nice quick turnaround. helps avoid more confusing stack traces for users. :+1:
